messages.subject: combine get_mon_arrival() with seized resources per customer
messages.subject_clean: combine get_mon_arrival() with seized resources per customer
messages.body_plain: The get_mon_arrival() function gives a table with an overview of the use of time for customers. Is there a way to include the number of seized resources for each customer in this table.
messages.body_snippet: The get_mon_arrival() function gives a table with an overview of the use of time for customers. Is there a way to include the number of seized resources for each customer in this table.

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] combine get_mon_arrival() with seized resources per customer
messages.subject_clean: [simmer-devel] combine get_mon_arrival() with seized resources per customer
messages.body_plain:
On Tue, 1 Mar 2022 at 16:14, Christian Andersen <casum...@gmail.com> wrote:
> The get_mon_arrival() function gives a table with an overview of the use of time for customers. Is there a way to include the number of seized resources for each customer in this table.
>

You can compute this from the info in the table:

get_mon_arrivals(env, per_resource = TRUE) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c("start_time", "end_time"), "var", values_to="time") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(time) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(name, replication) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(n_resources = cumsum(ifelse(var == "start_time", 1, -1))) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!duplicated(time, fromLast=TRUE)) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(name, time, n_resources, replication)

--
Iñaki Úcar

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Is there a way to create a copy of a Simulation Environment variable?
messages.subject_clean: [simmer-devel] Is there a way to create a copy of a Simulation Environment variable?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Thanks again for the suggestion. I parallelized the execution of my code using future.apply and the example on replication in the website (introduction to simmer) until time 50.

It runs ok, I did it for 10 replications. However I realized the individual runs need to be wrapped, which as you mentioned, keep the results but not the states, so still I cannot use them as restart points to later run scenarios from time 50 to 58.

Am I missing something? Is there a way to run the simulations in parallel and get links to each environment without wrapping them?

Thank you,
Luis

On Monday, February 28, 2022 at 2:28:51 PM UTC-7 Luis Acosta wrote:
> Thank you Iñaki! That’s could actually be a good workaround. I could pre-run several copies of the same simulation, have them ready for scenario forecasting when needed. I have not tried parallel in R in my machine yet, but I will do.
>
> I can see that saving/restoring simulations is not trivial. Anyway, this platform has been very helpful for my project so far, look forward to future developments.
>
> Cheers!
> Luis
>
> On Monday, February 28, 2022 at 3:46:38 AM UTC-7 iu...@fedoraproject.org wrote:
> > On Sat, 26 Feb 2022 at 00:09, Luis Acosta <acos...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > Hi,
> > >
> > > I just started using Simmer. I was wondering if there is a way to make a copy of a Simulation environment variable?
> > >
> > > The reason I would like to do this is because I am running a historic simulation that takes a few minutes (say stop time is 50), and then I would like to test different forecasting scenarios from time 50 to 58 which are much quicker. I wouldn’t want to re-run the full simulation every time I change forecasting parameters affecting period 50-58, I would like to run just from time 50 to 58.
> > >
> > > I was thinking that maybe I could just start each scenario by copying the historic simulation environment already run until time 50, so each time I change parameters and run it until time 58, I do not lose my original run until time 50.
> > >
> > > To make a copy of the simulation environment I tried a simple leftward assignment:
> > > Env_scen1 <- Env_hist
> > >
> > > However, it results in a link to the same object. So when I advance the simulation on Env_scen1, it advances it on Env_hist too.
> >
> > The simulation environment is a C++ object under the hood, so yes, assigning it to another variable just copies the reference to the same object. Unfortunately, currently there's no way to deep-copy a simulation (you can use the wrap method to just copy the results, but not the state, and a wrapped simulation is not runnable anymore). I agree this is an interesting feature, which requires the ability to (un)serialize, and more generally would allow us e.g. to save it to disk and restore it in another process or machine. But this is not a trivial problem and currently there's no roadmap for it.
> >
> > What you can do is to run your simulations in parallel. It may take a few minutes to reach t=50. But then, it takes the same amount of time for n processes to reach the same point separately, and from there, they could diverge in different scenarios.
> >
> > --
> > Iñaki Úcar

messages.subject: Determining arrivals based on sim time
messages.subject_clean: Determining arrivals based on sim time
messages.body_plain:
I'm modelling a contact centre. Part of the specs:
Simulate in minutes
generate arrivals each minute, based on rpois distribution
ensure that means of rpois differ for each hour in the day, e.g.
0 - 8: no calls
8 - 9: 5 calls
9 - 10: 21 calls
etc
My plan was to define a generator that calls a function that uses sim time (now(env)) as parameter
The function called then returns result of rpois with mean for the hour the sim time minute falls into.
I thought it was a great plan (and saw no alternatives obvious to me). The following skeleton code demonstrates the behaviour I'm trying to achieve:

arrivals <- function(sim_time) { return(sim_time * 2) }

env <- simmer()

t0 <- trajectory() %>%
  seize("resource") %>%
  timeout(1) %>%
  release("resource")

env %>% add_resource("resource", 1)
env %>% add_generator("Event", t0, function() { arrivals(now(env)) }, mon = 2 )

env %>%
  run(16)

The env loads, but running it (run(16)) immediately hangs

Q1: can now(env) be used in add_generator to retrieve sim time? If so what mistake am I making that I'm blind to?
Q2: if now(env) cannot be used this way; what would a better approach be to achieve my goal?

Many thanks!

messages.body_plain:
add_generator needs inter-arrival times, not number to generate at
time x - so at time zero, you're generating an infinite number of
arrivals (as the function returns zero)

tom

messages.body_plain:
Also, a common mistake is to use rpois to simulate a Poisson arrival process. This kind of process has exponential inter-arrival times, and given that simmer generators produce inter-arrival times, this means that you should use rexp instead.

You could also simulate a compound Poisson process, which consists of exponential inter-arrival times, and each arrival consists of a batch of size n, where n is Poisson distributed. To do this in simmer, you first need to generate an inter-arrival time with rexp (as in the previous case), and then append n-1 zeroes to that inter-arrival, where n is generated with rpois.

Iñaki
